title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues p.298 of the 'Longue Marche' sequel. There Grothendieck identified elliptic curves over C with a rigidification of unimodular form with points tau of the upper half-plane D. SL(2,Z) acts by Moebius transformations, effectively through SL(2,Z)' = PSL(2,Z) = GP(1,Z)^+, where GP(1,Z) = PGL(2,Z) = GL^pm(2,Z)' and a prime means quotient by +-1.

1. Critical orbits. The action is proper with exactly two critical orbits. One is the orbit of tau = i, where the lattice Z+Zi is the ring of integers of Q(i), with stabiliser of order 2. The other is the orbit of tau = j = exp(2 i pi/3), where Z+Zj is the ring of integers of Q(j), with stabiliser of order 3.

2. Formula (29). There is a canonical analytic, even algebraic, isomorphism D/PSL(2,Z) ~ P^1 minus {0} = Y. It is normalised so that the order-3 orbit goes to infinity and the order-2 orbit goes to 1; hence the cusp goes to the deleted point 0. In modern terms this is the coordinate 1728/j on the coarse moduli space of M_{1,1}: j(rho)=0 maps to infinity, j(i)=1728 maps to 1, and the cusp j=infinity maps to 0.

3. Formula (30). Set calG = GP(1,Z) = PGL(2,Z) and G = GP(1,Z)^+ = PSL(2,Z). Elements of determinant -1 act anti-holomorphically on D. Since D is contractible, the 'orbifold' fundamental group pi_1(D, calG, x) of D//calG is calG itself (base point x in D minus D^!, presumably the locus of points with non-trivial stabiliser). Grothendieck asserts an isomorphism of this group with pi_1^#(Y, d; y). Here d is the ramification datum: index 2 at 1, 3 at infinity, infinite at 0. The # apparently denotes the extended ('twisted') fundamental group that includes complex conjugation, Y being defined over R (indeed over Q).

4. Programme. He wants to make this explicit by writing the standard generators tau'_0, tau'_1, tau'_infinity as elements of PGL(2,Z). These satisfy tau_0 tau_1 tau_infinity = 1, tau_1^2 = 1 and tau_infinity^3 = 1. Classically tau_0 corresponds to T = [[1,1],[0,1]] and tau_1 to S = [[0,-1],[1,0]], with tau_infinity of order 3 (ST or its inverse), up to inversion and conventions. The extra generator is a reflection, e.g. diag(1,-1) or diag(-1,1).

5. Purpose. This prepares §39 (next page): the congruence conditions on the outer Galois action of Gamma_Q on hat-pi_{0,3}, via the comparison with M_{1,1} and GL(2, hat Z).
errors: No substantive mathematical error. Small imprecisions: the group acting effectively is PSL(2,Z), not SL(2,Z). He writes GP(1,Z)^+ = SL(2,Z)' (prime = mod +-1), which is consistent. The previous page's 'SL(2,Z) ~ GP(1,Z)^+' should be read modulo +-1.
The normalisation in (29) implicitly also requires the cusp to go to the deleted point 0; this is automatic but unstated.

pi_1(D, calG, x) = calG requires calG to include the anti-holomorphic (determinant -1) elements. The matching pi_1^# must then be the extended (real-structure) orbifold group, not the plain orbifold pi_1, which would give only PSL(2,Z).

ideas.what: Critical orbits of PSL(2,Z) on the upper half-plane correspond to CM by Z[i] and Z[rho], with ramification 2 and 3
ideas.modern_name: elliptic points of the modular group / CM points with extra automorphisms
ideas.where_published: M_{1,1} is discussed in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific statement is classical

ideas.what: D/PSL(2,Z) ~ P^1 minus {0}, normalised with order-3 point at infinity and order-2 point at 1 (i.e. coordinate 1728/j)
ideas.modern_name: j-invariant as the coarse moduli map of M_{1,1}

ideas.what: PGL(2,Z), including anti-holomorphic elements, as the extended orbifold fundamental group of (P^1; 0,1,infinity with indices infinity,2,3) with real structure
ideas.modern_name: orbifold/stack fundamental group of M_{1,1} over R; extended modular group as a Z/2 extension of Z/2*Z/3
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (extended modular group); orbifold formalism Thurston, Satake
ideas.where_published: Related material in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (twisted fundamental groups pi_1^#)

deep.surprise_reason: Classical identification of the modular orbifold and its extended fundamental group, written as preparation for the Galois-action computation of §39. The only personal touches are the normalisation 1728/j with points (0,1,infinity) and the pi_1^# notation. Nothing appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'GL(1,Z)' in (29) and the following line should read 'GP(1,Z)' (Grothendieck's notation for PGL(2,Z)); thus calG = GP(1,Z), G = GP(1,Z)^+ = SL(2,Z)'.
The marginal '(p.ex[?])' before calG = ... is more plausibly '(posant'.
'l'anneau [?] réseau des entiers alg.': 'l'anneau' appears to be a false start replaced by 'réseau'.
The final marginal remark reads '(analytiques, et même algébriques)' qualifying the isomorphism (29).
